instruction: Download the HTML source of https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/searching and save it as 'searching.html' on the Desktop.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated to Apple HIG searching page, scrolled to understand content structure, opened terminal, used curl to download HTML, installed python-docx and beautifulsoup4, wrote a Python script to extract content between 'Searching' and 'Resources' sections, created notes.docx on Desktop. File was created (36KB) but content/formatting did not match the gold standard docx.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome to specific URLs, scroll web pages, open terminal, use curl to download files, install pip packages, write and execute Python scripts, create files on Desktop
metadata.failure_analysis: Model successfully created a docx file but the content extraction via regex and plain-text formatting did not match the gold standard document. The compare_docx_files evaluator found the documents too different despite fuzzy matching.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified the original task from content extraction + docx conversion to just downloading the raw HTML file. The model demonstrated it can use curl to download the page (it did this as an intermediate step). This tests a subset of the original capability without the complex content extraction.
metadata.explanation: Task requires downloading the Apple HIG searching page as HTML to the Desktop. Custom getter reads the file from VM and extracts content. Custom metric checks: file exists (0.3), exceeds minimum size (0.2), and contains expected keywords (0.5 proportional).

scoring_breakdown.keywords: 0.5 - Content contains expected keywords (searching, best practices, search field, systemwide search, platform considerations)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads file from /home/user/Desktop/searching.html via env.controller.get_file() and returns existence, size, and lowercased content
Metric correctly accesses expected parameter directly (expected.get('min_size'), expected.get('keywords')) — proper handling for type='rule' where get_rule returns rules dict
Scoring breakdown is reasonable: file exists (0.3), min size check (0.2), keyword proportion (0.5) = 1.0 max
Case-insensitive keyword matching (content lowered, keywords lowered in comparison) is appropriate for HTML content verification
Complete coverage: instruction requires download + save, evaluator verifies file existence, size, and content authenticity via keywords

Keywords ('searching', 'best practices', 'search field', 'systemwide search', 'platform considerations') are plausible for the Apple HIG searching page but cannot be definitively verified without live page access
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a check for HTML structure (e.g., presence of <html> or <!DOCTYPE> tags) to ensure the file is actual HTML rather than an error page or redirect
Keyword list accuracy depends on the actual page content at download time — if the page structure changes, some keywords may not be present
